content:
maria: FYI, we've got an escalation from AcadiaHealth — p99 latency jumped ~4x after the runtime rollout at ~09:12 UTC. Customer reported generation requests timing out or taking multiple seconds. Requesting triage.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed: runtime-v2.14 -> 30% traffic at 09:10 UTC :rocket:

devon: on it. which endpoints? any error rates? logs?

maria: endpoint /v1/generate (text-gen). No error spike, just tail latency. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~450ms (was ~200), p99 ~1.8s (was ~400ms). Grafana: <https://grafana/reports/latency?panel=acadia>.

julian: interesting. any model or kernel changes in v2.14? which kernel selector landed?

ash: commit abc1234 changed kernel selector fallback ordering and added a "safety" single-thread fallback when perf signals jitter. Might be related.

devon: I can see the tail in canary logs. `kubectl logs -l canary=runtime-v2.14 -c runtime --tail=200` shows repeated snippets: 

```
WARN KV_CACHE: miss_count=4327 prefix_key_misses=120
WARN kernel_selector: fallback to cpu_kernel for layer 12, reason=jit_timeout
latency_ms=1823 req_id=...
```

maria: support says Acadia uses longer sequences (avg 800 tokens) — that could exacerbate JIT/runtime kernel choices.

julian: that fits. longer seq -> different kernel path. New selector may pick an optimized fp32 kernel that triggers JIT compile + timeouts, which then falls back to slow cpu path.

devon: I reproduced a tail with their payload against canary. `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate -d @payload.json` produced similar p99s. Attached payload to thread.

support-ops: tagging the customer to acknowledge: @acadia-health we're investigating, will update in 90m :white_check_mark:

ash: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback that shard to v2.13, 2) force kernel selector override via env `RUNTIME_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_optimized` for that pool, or 3) increase JIT timeout. Thoughts?

maria: customer needs immediate relief. I'd rather try kernel override first (less disruptive) and prepare rollback if it fails.

devon: I'm patching the canary config to pin the kernel policy for the Acadia pool. Pushing flag now.

deploy-bot: Deploy request accepted: runtime-v2.14-canary -> patch kernel_override applied to pool "acadia-pool" :white_check_mark:

julian: starting a bisect on the commit range abc1200..abc1245 to find the regression point.

devon: repro steps I used: 
```
1) export ACADIA_PAYLOAD=payload.json
2) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate -d @$ACADIA_PAYLOAD -o /tmp/out.json
3) jq .meta.latency_ms /tmp/out.json
4) run 200 iterations, compute p95/p99
```

ash: after applying kernel_override, canary p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms. Rolling override to the customer's pool now.

maria: timeline / action items: 
- rollback evaluated -> kernel override applied, customer pinged (maria)
- julian to finish bisect and identify offending commit
- devon to collect KV cache stats + sequence distribution
- ash to prepare hotfix to prevent cpu_kernel fallback on long sequences
- send postmortem template when resolved (sre-bot)

sre-bot: Created incident IR-2140000000, severity: sev2, runbook: latency-regression.

ian: perf traces show spikes in `jit_compile()` threads. Flamegraph link: <https://perf/graphs/2140000000/flame>. Looks like JIT compile latency correlates with the slow requests.

julian: bisect narrowed it down to commit abc1234 — the kernel selector reorder + safety fallback. Reverting that commit on a test pool returns p99 to baseline.

devon: proposed fix: revert the safety fallback and instead increase GPU JIT timeout for large-memory cards and add telemetry for fallback counts. PR ready: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4598

maria: customer update sent: "Thanks — p99 looks normal now. We'll validate overnight." :relieved:

ash: follow-ups: add e2e test for long-sequence workloads, add per-request JIT-fallback telemetry, and gate rollout on fallback-rate threshold.

sre-bot: Action log: 
- 09:14 kernel_override applied, p99 improved
- 09:30 PR #4598 opened (revert + timeout change)
- 09:45 customer notified
Owners: maria (customer comms), julian (bisect/fix), devon (repro/metrics), ash (patch), ian (perf)

support-ops: we'll close the customer loop in 24h, reopen if anything pops up.

maria: thanks all — postmortem draft incoming.
